description:
FOUND s499 (Fable, 2026-09-27) by the s496a merge-review probes (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/review/f-unicode-classes.pl; out/f-unicode-classes.{perl,base,tree}.out).  PRE-EXISTING: identical on main 1b0baa7c and on the s496a tree 0ab64a45 (the #2060 batch added the property TABLES but did not touch the six built-in classes).

THE TABLE (perl 5.40.3 -> PCL; the string is a wide/utf8 string in every row):
    "\x{663}"  =~ /\d/           1 -> 0     (ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT THREE is Nd)
    "\x{ff11}" =~ /\d/           1 -> 0     (FULLWIDTH DIGIT ONE)
    "\x{663}"  =~ /(?u)\d/       1 -> 0
    "\x{663}"  =~ /[[:digit:]]/  1 -> 0
    "\x{663}"  =~ /\D/           0 -> 1
    split /\d/, "a\x{663}b"      2 fields -> 1 field   (the value flows onward: a SILENT WRONG)
    "\x{2003}" =~ /\s/           1 -> 0     (EM SPACE; NBSP U+00A0 IS matched -- so \s is a hand list, not perl`s class)
    "\x{301}"  =~ /\w/           1 -> 0     (a combining mark is \w in perl: \p{Word} = Alnum + M + Pc + Join_Control)
  and the OTHER direction, perl`s byte/utf8 string model (not a PCL bug to fix here; PCL has one string kind):
    "\x{e9}" =~ /\w/             0 -> 1     (perl: a NON-utf8 string uses ASCII rules for \w without `use feature "unicode_strings"`; under `use utf8`/decoded input perl answers 1 too)
    "a\x{e9}" =~ /a\x{e9}\b/     0 -> 1     (same cause)

WHERE: cl/vendor/cl-ppcre/util.lisp:109-140 -- `digit-char-p` is `(char<= #\0 chr #\9)` (ASCII), `word-char-p` is alphanumericp + `_` (SBCL`s alphanumericp: Unicode letters/digits, but NOT marks, NOT Pc), `whitespacep` is a fixed list; convert.lisp:103-108 maps :digit-class / :word-char-class / :whitespace-char-class to them.  The POSIX class [[:digit:]] takes the same route.

FIX SHAPE (measure first): now that #2060 ships perl`s own inversion lists lazily, the three predicates can be perl`s -- `\p{Nd}` (`Digit`), `\p{XPosixSpace}` (`Space`), `\p{Word}` -- WITH AN ASCII FAST PATH so the common case does not pay the binary search: `(if (< code 128) <the ASCII test> (%pcl-invlist-member-p code <list>))`.  The lists must not force the uniprops extension to LOAD for an all-ASCII program: load it on the first NON-ASCII character that reaches the slow arm (the extension is FASL-cached, #1202).  /a (`(?a)`, `use re "/a"`) keeps the ASCII test.  BENCH: regexg / textproc / subste must not move > 1 % (the fast path is one compare + branch).  The byte-string rows (\x{e9}) are perl`s "Unicode bug" and stay as they are unless not-supported.md`s string-model section is re-scoped -- cite it.
BAR: cl/ change => full sweep (re/ and op/split rows with non-ASCII digits are candidate movers), companion re/ + op/ legs, guard rows in an existing regex Pl/t file (inverse-verified), the bench control with load.
PRIORITY: low-medium (real programs with non-ASCII digits/spaces are rare; the split row is the silent-wrong that matters).
=== NOTE (s494u, #2092 phase 1 -- the shared mechanism) ===
The /a arm now lives in the ONE rewrite scan: %pcl-rx-scan-step's escape branch asks %pcl-rx-ascii-escape-text when (rxs-a s) is set (the struct carries a / astack, tracked through inline (?a) / (?^...) groups exactly like x / xstack, and perl-regex-to-ppcre takes the trailing /a as its third argument; the scan's pre-test adds "a in force AND a \w \W \s \S \b \B is present").  #2440's /u fix is the OTHER arm of that same branch: when (rxs-a s) is NIL, \d \D \s \S (and \w for marks) become their Unicode forms (\p{Nd}/\p{XPosixSpace}/\p{Word}, inside a class the \p spelling, outside a bracketed one), with the pre-test widened accordingly -- do not add a second table or a second scan.  Under /a they must stay ASCII (\s = [\t\n\x0B\f\r\x20], which already includes VT).  Mind the cost: today a pattern with no \h\v\R\X\N\p, no possessive, no loose {,n} and no (*F) is NOT scanned at all; #2440 would scan every pattern holding \d \s or \w, so keep an ASCII fast path (the scan runs once per distinct pattern text -- cached -- but the resulting \p classes are slower to match than cl-ppcre's native ones; measure regexg/subste/textproc).
subject: `\d` `\D` `[[:digit:]]` are ASCII-only, `\s` misses U+2003 (EM SPACE), `\w` misses combining marks (U+0301) on WIDE strings where perl 5.40.3 uses its Unicode classes -- SILENT no-match / wrong split count; answerable from the #2060 tables (\p{Nd} \p{XPosixSpace} \p{Word}) with an ASCII fast path
